sections.title: Day, then part of day, then clock time
sections.content: You already know how to say a day (hétfőn), a part of the day (reggel, este) and a clock time (hétkor). Hungarian happily stacks all three in that order — day, then part of day, then exact time — to pin something down precisely.

items.english: On Monday morning at nine I work.
On Tuesday evening at seven I have Hungarian class.

sections.content: Nothing new is happening grammatically — you're just putting three things you already know how to say next to each other, in the order Hungarian expects them.
